name: Porechop
description: adapter trimmer for Oxford Nanopore reads

parameters.name: barcode_threshold
parameters.label: Percent identity for binning
parameters.help: A read must have at least this percent identity to a barcode to be binned (default: 75.0)

parameters.name: barcode_diff
parameters.label: Minimum difference in identity
parameters.help: If the difference between a read's best barcode identity and its second-best barcode identity is less than this value, it will not be put in a barcode bin (to exclude cases which are too close to call) (default: 5.0)

parameters.name: require_two_barcodes
parameters.label: Require two matches for binning
parameters.help: Reads will only be put in barcode bins if they have a strong match for the barcode on both their start and end (default: a read can be binned with a match at its start or end)

parameters.name: discard_unassigned
parameters.label: Discard unassigned reads
parameters.help: Discard unassigned reads (instead of creating a 'none' bin) (default: False)

parameters.name: adapter_threshold
parameters.label: Minimum identity
parameters.help: An adapter set has to have at least this percent identity to be labelled as present and trimmed off (0 to 100) (default: 90.0)

parameters.name: check_reads
parameters.label: Number of alligned reads
parameters.help: This many reads will be aligned to all possible adapters to determine which adapter sets are present (default: 10000)

parameters.name: scoring_scheme
parameters.label: Scoring scheme
parameters.help: Comma-delimited string of alignment scores: match, mismatch, gap open, gap extend

validators.message: Scoring scheme must be comma-separated string of four positive/negative integers

parameters.name: end_size
parameters.label: Number of bases
parameters.help: The number of base pairs at each end of the read which will be searched for adapter sequences (default: 150)

parameters.name: min_trim_size
parameters.label: Minimum trim length
parameters.help: Adapter alignments smaller than this will be ignored (default: 4)

parameters.name: extra_end_trim
parameters.label: Extra bases trimmed
parameters.help: This many additional bases will be removed next to adapters found at the ends of reads (default: 2)

parameters.name: end_threshold
parameters.label: Minimum percent identity
parameters.help: Adapters at the ends of reads must have at least this percent identity to be removed (0 to 100) (default: 75.0)

parameters.name: no_split
parameters.label: Skip splitting
parameters.help: Skip splitting reads based on middle adapters (default: split reads when an adapter is found in the middle)

parameters.name: discard_middle
parameters.label: Discard reads with middle adapter
parameters.help: Reads with middle adapters will be discarded (default: reads with middle adapters are split) (required for reads to be used with Nanopolish, this option is on by default when outputting reads into barcode bins)

parameters.name: middle_threshold
parameters.label: Minimum percent identity
parameters.help: Adapters in the middle of reads must have at least this percent identity to be found (0 to 100) (default: 85.0)

parameters.name: extra_middle_trim_good_side
parameters.label: Extra trimming good side
parameters.help: This many additional bases will be removed next to middle adapters on their 'good' side (default: 10)

parameters.name: extra_middle_trim_bad_side
parameters.label: Extra trimming bad side
parameters.help: This many additional bases will be removed next to middle adapters on their 'bad' side (default: 100)

parameters.name: min_split_read_size
parameters.label: Minimum length reads post-split
parameters.help: Post-split read pieces smaller than this many base pairs will not be outputted (default: 1000)

inputs.name: log_file
inputs.label: Generate log file
inputs.help: Generates a log file out of stdout, which can be used as MultiQC input

help.content:
Porechop is a tool for finding and removing adapters from Oxford Nanopore reads.
Adapters on the ends of reads are trimmed off, and when a read has an adapter in
its middle, it is treated as chimeric and chopped into separate reads. Porechop
performs thorough alignments to effectively find adapters, even at low sequence identity.

Porechop also supports demultiplexing of Nanopore reads that were barcoded with
the Native Barcoding Kit, PCR Barcoding Kit or Rapid Barcoding Kit.
